The onset of Delhi’s fabled winter once began with the saptaparni. The potent fragrance of the Alstonia scholaris, or the Indian devil tree, was meant to drive one to madness. But, accompanied as it was by a pleasant chill in the night air, the torturous summer and monsoon firmly in the past, it only ever signalled joy to Dilliwalis. Now, the honeyed scent sets off a different kind of madness: If the saptaparni has bloomed, can the arrival of the season of deadly air be far behind?
